gates.test @openpacker/opm-project: pass (223 tests; was 217 — added 5 delegated cache tests in host-fetch.test.ts and 1 first-party npm cache test in registry.test.ts)
gates.test @openpacker/opm: pass (26 tests; the repeat opmx --plugin run now asserts fetches === 1 and the '(cached)' stderr line)

notes: DEFECT FIXED: the ephemeral tool cache never hit (present since a1759a5, all ecosystems). fetchTool always passed downloaded bytes to materializeLockPackage, so the content-addressed store archive was never consulted and opmx's '(cached)' line was unreachable. FIX SHAPE: resolution is now metadata-first via the new resolveRegistryArtifactDeferred (packages/opm-project/src/registry.ts) — same provider/inspect/fail-closed checks as resolveRegistryArtifact (which was refactored to share the descriptor-read, identity, and origin-allowlist helpers; behavior unchanged, all existing registry tests green unmodified). NETWORK CALLS PER REPEAT RUN (unchanged, intentionally — resolution is NOT cached): enumerate (unpinned purls only), inspect (twice: descriptor resolution + supply-chain fact capture), registry-definition reads, and fetch-artifact-record for delegated providers (cheap metadata over the bounded stdio protocol). SKIPPED ON A CACHE HIT: the artifact byte download — the host-side HTTPS fetch for delegated providers, and for first-party providers the fetch-artifact-record call itself when the inspection publishes the full artifact descriptor (sha256 digest + size + location; the npm adapter does this when dist.integrity carries a sha256 SRI and dist.size is present — real registries publishing only sha512 SRI fall back to the old record-carries-bytes path). On a first-party fallback the record is read once and its bytes are used (no double download). CACHE TRUST MODEL: the store is keyed by the freshly resolved digest (storePathForDigest); a hit re-reads the .artifact archive and re-hashes it against that digest inside materializeLockPackage before rebuilding the tree — exactly the install.ts lock-replay treatment, so a tampered tree is rebuilt from the verified archive and a tampered archive falls through to the bounded download + verify and self-heals (archive rewritten with verified bytes). A missing archive with a surviving tree is NOT trusted (tree alone proves nothing) and re-downloads. A registry that re-pins the digest is a miss for the new digest. Bins on a hit come from the fresh inspection's declared executables (pkg.bins) or discovery over the rebuilt tree, as before. POLICY: new bindVerifiedArtifactCacheEntry (install.ts) binds the freshly captured facts through the verified-capability WeakMap without bytes, so the cache-path policy gate evaluates the same fresh facts as a download run; registryArtifactVerified still means bytes are hashed against what the registry just published (the archive read does it), and facts still cannot be hand-authored from stored data (the layer-01 invariant test at opm-project.test.ts:794 stays green). Runtime-closure deps get the same treatment automatically — they flow through the same materialiseExact helper; the walk's soft-fail semantics are unchanged. DOCS RESTORED: ephemeral.ts module docstring, opmx help text, and docs/guides/opm.md now state the true behavior (metadata always re-resolved; bytes content-addressed cached; '(cached)' reported). TESTS CHANGED THAT ASSERTED THE OLD BEHAVIOR: exactly one — apps/opm/test/opm.test.ts 'acquires and runs a plugin-served native tool' (the repeat-run block asserted fetches === 2 and no '(cached)'; now asserts fetches === 1 and /\(cached\)/). No other existing test was modified.
deviations: Scope allowed packages/opm-project plus apps/opm tests; the fix also touched apps/opm/src/opmx.ts help text and docs/guides/opm.md because restoring the doc claims was explicitly in scope. One new exported helper each in registry.ts (resolveRegistryArtifactDeferred) and install.ts (bindVerifiedArtifactCacheEntry); no changes to existing exported signatures. First-party byte-download skipping is opportunistic by design: it requires the inspection to publish a usable sha256 artifact descriptor (npm with sha256 SRI + size qualifies; sha512-only packuments still download per run — the digest cannot be known metadata-only there, and working around that would mean caching resolution, which is explicitly out of bounds).
